items.fullText: AI·SW SW 아이티센피엔에스, AI 보안 사업 확장…AI 운영 환경 전반 보호 발행일 : 2026-11-23 11:47 전자신문을 선호 매체로 추가 공유하기 페이스북 X(트위터) X(트위터) --> 메일 URL 복사 글자크기 설정 가 작게 가 보통 가 크게 아이티센 사옥 전경. 아이티세피엔에스는 기업의 인공지능(AI) 활용 확대에 따라 새롭게 등장하는 보안 위협에 대응하기 위해 AI 보안 사업을 확장한다. 아이티센그룹의 보안 전문기업 아이티센피엔에스는 AI 모델과 애플리케이션, 데이터, AI 에이전트 등 AI 운영 환경 전반을 보호하는 통합 AI 보안 사업을 강화한다고 23일 밝혔다. 최근 글로벌 사이버보안 시장은 AI를 활용해 사이버 위협을 탐지하고 대응하는 기술과 함께, 기업이 도입하는 AI 모델과 애플리케이션, 데이터 및 AI 에이전트까지 보호하는 방향으로 빠르게 확대되고 있다. 이 같은 변화는 글로벌 보안기업들의 투자 전략에서도 나타나고 있다. 아이티센피엔에스가 국내 총판을 맡고 있는 팔로알토 네트웍스는 최근 오픈 웨이트 AI 모델의 추가 학습과 추론을 지원하는 AI 플랫폼 기업 어플라이드 컴퓨트를 약 45억 달러 규모에 인수하는 계약을 체결했다. 아이티센피엔에스는 이러한 시장 변화에 맞춰 기존의 AI 기반 위협 탐지·대응 역량을 기업의 AI 운영 환경 자체를 보호하는 영역으로 확대한다는 전략이다. 개별 보안 솔루션 공급을 넘어 AI 모델과 애플리케이션의 취약점 검증부터 데이터 및 접근 권한 보호, 운영 단계의 위협 탐지·대응까지 연계하는 통합 보안 사업을 강화할 방침이다. 이를 위해 'AI 시큐리티 이노베이션 센터'를 중심으로 AI 보안 기술 검증과 컨설팅, 공격형 보안, 솔루션 구축 및 운영 역량을 결합하고 있다. 글로벌 보안기업의 통합 보안 플랫폼과 전문 보안 파트너의 공격 검증 기술을 연계해 고객의 AI 도입 환경에 적합한 보안 체계를 제공한다는 구상이다. 아울러 기업의 외부 노출 자산과 취약점을 식별하고 실제 공격자 관점에서 위험성을 검증하는 공격형 보안 역량을 AI 기반 위협 탐지·분석·대응 체계와 연계한다. 박원규 아이티센피엔에스 대표는 “앞으로의 보안은 개별 솔루션을 도입하는 수준을 넘어 AI 모델과 데이터, 애플리케이션, 아이덴티티, 인프라 등 전체 운영 환경을 지속적으로 검증하고 보호하는 방향으로 발전해야 한다”며 “아이티센피엔에스는 글로벌 보안 기술과 자체 AI 보안 역량, 전문 파트너 생태계를 결합해 기업이 AI를 도입하는 단계부터 실제 업무에 활용하는 운영 단계까지 일관된 보안 체계를 제공하겠다”고 말했다. 강성전 기자 castlekang@etnews.com

items.fullText: Markets Markets plunge: Nasdaq erases 2026 gains, S&P and Dow enter corrections Anthropic’s record-setting IPO Thursday failed to restore investor confidence in the AI market. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Stock markets plunge as Nasdaq erases 2026 gains 01:54 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 20, 2026, 9:20 AM EST / Updated Nov. 20, 2026, 4:37 PM EST By Rob Wile The surging stock market of 2026 capsized Friday, wiping out gains for the year in the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite while the broad S&P 500 and the Dow entered correction territory, meaning they have declined 10% from recent peaks. The dramatic sell-off is raising fresh fears about the viability of the AI investment wave that had powered stocks and economic growth for the first half of the year. Friday’s declines were led by Anthropic, whose blockbuster IPO just 24 hours earlier now feels like a blip after the stock lost 9%, wiping out hundreds of billions in paper wealth and putting shares just a few dollars above the IPO price. Nvidia also dragged markets lower, tumbling about 14% following a Reuters report that regulators are looking into accounting irregularities at the chip giant. With Friday’s losses of 3.7%, the S&P 500’s seven-day losing streak is its worst since the Covid pandemic; the index is now up less than 1% on the year. The Nasdaq finished the day down 5.3%, and the Dow dropped 1.9%. The losses also sully one of the most visible bright points of President Donald Trump’s second term. Amid sticky inflation and frozen housing and jobs markets, U.S. equities were the one part of the economy that appeared resilient. The AI investment boom created seemingly insatiable demand for stocks among investors, minting multiple new trillion-dollar companies in the process. Turning a simulation idea into a working application means assembling assets, connecting physics and rendering, and checking that the scene behaves as intended. Developers are combining frontier AI models with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to help carry out that work — building applications for exploring scenarios, investigating failures and improving designs. Developers direct AI agents through natural-language instructions, review results and guide changes. Omniverse libraries provide GPU-accelerated physics, rendering and sensor simulation capabilities. Explore the projects below to see frontier AI models such as GPT-6 Astra at work, and check back for new examples from NVIDIA teams and developers across the ecosystem. They use industrial tools and engineering data to help engineers build digital twins that test plans and processes and evaluate operational decisions. Falkor, a KONGSBERG company, shows how this works in practice. The company’s Falkor Surface platform lets customers turn their computer-aided design and engineering data into facility-scale digital twins using the GPT-6 Astra model. The platform uses NVIDIA Omniverse libraries and NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Server Edition GPUs on Microsoft Azure to enable advanced physics simulation. items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Another AI company is about to be worth more than $1 trillion. What that means for the rest of us. Anthropic’s public market debut comes as the AI investment boom stands at a crossroads. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Anthropic co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei in Washington, in September. Finn Gomez / Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 18, 2026, 4:13 PM EST / Updated Nov. 18, 2026, 4:23 PM EST By Rob Wile Leading AI lab Anthropic is expected to make the largest-ever public market debut when it starts trading on the Nasdaq stock exchange Thursday. Founded in 2021 by brother and sister Dario and Daniela Amodei, both former employees of rival OpenAI, Anthropic and its main product, Claude, are seen as the gold standard of AI models, despite lacking the household name cache of ChatGPT. With a target market value of $1.5 trillion — larger than SpaceX’s record setting IPO just a few months ago — Anthropic’s public arrival will serve as more than just a measure of what Wall Street thinks the company is worth. It will be a test of current sentiment around AI itself at a pivotal moment for the industry. For much of the past year, the AI investment wave has powered the stock market to new heights and sustained U.S. economic growth. But there are signs the wave may be starting to break. “Investors have over recent weeks become increasingly concerned around the sustainability of the investment boom,” James McCann, senior economist for investment strategy at Edward Jones, said in a client note Wednesday ahead of Anthropic’s debut. The market gains notched in the spring and summer thanks to the AI boom have now largely been wiped out. Fears of overspending on infrastructure, rising debt loads, ballooning costs and uncertain demand have grown. New NVIDIA RTX Spark compact desktops from ASUS, Dell and MSI are available today, bringing local AI agents, image and video generation, and model fine-tuning to a dedicated Windows PC. With up to 128GB of unified memory and NVIDIA’s AI software stack, these systems provide room for larger local models alongside RTX-accelerated creative and development tools. A dedicated desktop can keep agents and scheduled tasks running while a laptop travels or handles other work. Alongside the new desktops, an expanding software ecosystem brings more creative and development workflows to RTX Spark laptops and compact desktops. Native Windows on Arm applications from Adobe, the NVIDIA DLSS Ray Reconstruction feature in Blender and local generation workflows in ComfyUI expand what creators and developers can do on RTX Spark — all on one Windows PC. A Windows PC Built for Local AI As workflows expand to include local AI models and agents, more work can continue beyond an active editing session — from generating assets to processing long renders or scheduled tasks. RTX Spark compact desktops give developers, creators and AI enthusiasts a dedicated Windows PC for local models and always-on agents. They bring together image and video generation, model fine-tuning, creative applications and development tools in one compact system. Running supported models locally keeps locally processed code and files on the PC and avoids per-token cloud application programming interface (API) charges for those tasks. items.fullText: Ian Buck Kicks Off NVIDIA’s Week at SC26 as Science Enters the Age of Agents At SC26, NVIDIA’s VP of Hyperscale and HPC laid out how researchers can combine simulation, AI and agents to accelerate scientific discovery. November 17, 2026 by Brian Caulfield 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA’s Ian Buck kicked off the company’s week at SC26 in Chicago on Monday with new tools for AI agents, software that can plan experiments, run code and check results on researchers’ own systems. In NVIDIA’s special address, Buck announced Nemotron for Science , the Rubin HPC GPU and an expanded Vera CPU platform for high-performance computing . He also detailed a new collaboration in quantum computing with IBM and Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory . “The frontier of computing and the new scientific stack is going to be simulation, as always, but combined with AI and the future of quantum,” said Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. Buck opened the talk by looking back to his first public talk on CUDA, at an SC06 tutorial in Tampa, Florida, 20 years ago. NVIDIA now offers more than 1,000 CUDA-X libraries , he said. Open Models for Science Agents “[Agents] have been just a game changer in how we interface with our supercomputers, with our devices, our instruments and how we can do the research,” Buck said. Simulation remains the foundation of scientific computing, “which will always be on the top,” Buck said, with AI, quantum and now agents working alongside it. Nemotron for Science combines the Nemotron 3.5 Super VL open model with a new open chemistry dataset and post-training recipes for life sciences and chemistry, Buck explained. Researchers can run it locally on a DGX Spark, a workstation or their own supercomputer. items.fullText: NVIDIA Sweeps MLPerf Training and Endpoints as Vera Rubin Debuts With Leading Performance November 16, 2026 by Shruti Koparkar 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! In its MLPerf benchmarks debut, with results released today, the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform delivers leading performance across training, post-training and agentic inference. NVIDIA swept every MLPerf Training v6.1 benchmark and, in its first MLPerf Endpoints submission, delivered more than 10x generational gains in throughput per watt for agentic AI — measuring how much agentic work a system delivers with each watt of power. These results are just the beginning. Vera Rubin performance will keep climbing through continuous optimization of NVIDIA’s CUDA-powered software stack , so the infrastructure that customers invest in today delivers more value over time. NVIDIA Sweeps MLPerf Training v6.1 AI agents are now everywhere, writing code, running business workflows, answering customer questions and, as this week’s SC26 conference highlights , advancing scientific research. Faster training means smarter agents can reach users sooner, drug discovery models can keep pace with new lab data and fraud-detection models can adapt to new threats faster. MLPerf Training measures how fast a system can train a range of AI models to a target level of accuracy. The NVIDIA platform was the only one with results on every benchmark this round, spanning large language models, image generation, recommender systems and reinforcement learning post-training. In its debut, Vera Rubin NVL72 delivered up to 2x more performance per GPU than the highly optimized NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 system — early results that show the pace of generation-over-generation innovation. With expanded NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries, including cuPhoton, cuPotential and cuSpa, researchers can sift through vast amounts of data to accelerate research, from astrophysics and materials science to single-cell biology. The speedups are helping scientists analyze larger datasets and model more complex systems. The new libraries give AI agents the tools to help researchers make discoveries faster than ever. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Bringing Black Holes Into Focus Seeing a black hole takes a telescope the size of Earth. The Event Horizon Telescope links radio dishes worldwide, generating petabytes of data that can take months to process. With NVIDIA cuPhoton.xBeam, a module within the cuPhoton Toolkit , black hole observations from the Event Horizon Telescope can now be correlated orders of magnitude faster than ever. Analysis that once took over a month now takes eight minutes. By combining global radio dishes into Earth-sized aperture, cuPhoton delivers unprecedented astronomical imaging resolution. cuPhoton successfully correlated observations of powerful black hole jets J1924 and 3C279 in the night sky — making it a reality to reconstruct a Messier 87* black hole galaxy in real time. The entire pipeline, from data loading and processing to visualization, runs on distributed multi-GPU systems or a compact NVIDIA DGX Spark system, helping scientists study how gas spirals inward under a black hole’s powerful gravitational pull. Steering Fusion Simulations Sustaining plasma at millions of degrees is essential to achieving stable, continuous fusion energy. But simulating its behavior is costly: on petascale systems, a single time step can take days, with simulations running for weeks. items.fullText: AI Day Seoul Brings Together Korea’s Industry Leaders, Startups and Developer Communities November 15, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Over two days at COEX, more than 2,000 attendees converged for AI Day Seoul, bringing together Korea’s industry leaders, startups and developer communities advancing physical AI and AI agents. At the plenary sessions, Deepu Talla, vice president of robotics and edge AI at NVIDIA, said Korea is “punching above its weight,” with Doosan Robotics, Hyundai Motor Group, LG Electronics and SK Group — as well as startups like Real World and Luda Robotics — using NVIDIA platforms to bring general-purpose robotics into the real world. Jonathan Cohen, vice president of applied research at NVIDIA, showed how enterprises can build agents they own and control. Breakout sessions featured speakers from Coupang Intelligent Cloud, Doosan Robotics, LG AI Research, LG Electronics, NAVER Cloud, SK Telecom and Upstage. “It was a genuinely enjoyable time to have candid conversations,” said Hyunho Yang, research engineer for omnimodal foundation models at SK Telecom. “Seeing the passion of fellow AI developers was a real source of inspiration for me.” Community leaders share how they build with open models and tools at AI Day Seoul. The Agentic AI 10x Bootcamp Community Day brought together Pseudo Lab, Python Korea, PyTorchKR, HAERAE, Hugging Face KREW, Graph User Group, Womxn Who Code Korea, Dnol (Datayanolja) and other developer communities. Five finalists from the Hangul Day hackathon, co-hosted with Fastcampus, built agents trained on the Korean language and culture with the OpenShell runtime. The winning team, FlyGate, received an NVIDIA DGX Spark system. More than 500 developers also took part in full-day NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute workshops and NVIDIA Certification exams in Korean.
